title: Should the spec clarify that character encoding declarations are not actually required?

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

body:
Hello. I recently submitted an issue on the inclusion of `<meta charset="utf-8">` in examples of the specification. I was informed that character encoding declarations are not required in a document:

> A character encoding declaration is not required for conformant HTML. What is required is that *if* you include one, its contents be `utf-8`. But you don't have to include one.

_Originally posted by @domenic in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8726#issuecomment-1382032709_

However, there is a note in the [section on character encoding declarations](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#charset) suggesting that they are required:

> A character encoding declaration is required (either in the [Content-Type metadata](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#content-type) or explicitly in the file) even when all characters are in the ASCII range, because a character encoding is needed to process non-ASCII characters entered by the user in forms, in URLs generated by scripts, and so forth.
>
> Using non-UTF-8 encodings can have unexpected results on form submission and URL encodings, which use the [document's character encoding](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding) by default.

Should this language be changed to reflect the fact that character encoding declarations are not actually required? I apologize if I am misunderstanding the specification in some way.
